summary: Public primary-source discovery found New Jersey role-scope guidance useful for a draft ED-to-admission authority matrix, but no public source supplies current RWJUH or Saint Peter’s privilege rosters, facility bylaws, role-specific admission orders, or credential expiry data. Treat state scope rules as candidate constraints and send facility-specific rules for institutional review. This is source discovery, not dataset acquisition.

sources.title: Physician Assistant Frequently Asked Questions
sources.publisher: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs, Physician Assistant Advisory Committee
sources.period: Page accessed 2026-10-10; the listed FAQ includes a 2023 modification date. Verify current law before operational use.
sources.grain: Public FAQ statements about PA licensure, delegation agreements and supervision
useful_fields: PA practice requires physician supervision (FAQ wording should be checked against current law)
delegated services are bounded by the agreement, supervising physician specialty, competence and training
FAQ states a maximum supervisory ratio of four PAs per physician at one time
observed_facts: Search result text reports that a PA practice relationship requires a written delegation agreement and that delegation is limited by specialty and competence.
Search result text reports a supervisory ratio of no more than four PAs to one physician at a time.
Direct page open returned HTTP 403 in the research tool; these findings are search-result observations, not independently inspected page text.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Authorized researcher should retrieve and preserve the current page or controlling statutes/rules, record retrieval date and document version, and have institutional counsel/faculty validate the rule before using it in the matrix.
limitations: Could not inspect the page directly (403).
State-level role scope does not establish facility appointment, service-specific privileges, ED assignment, admission authority, or local supervision coverage.
Do not derive eligibility from NPI records.

sources.title: Determining Scope of Nursing Practice Model
sources.publisher: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs, Board of Nursing
sources.period: Page accessed 2026-10-10; current validity not established because direct open failed.
sources.grain: Guidance for evaluating whether a nursing act is within scope and authorized in context
useful_fields: scope under nursing act and regulations
valid order or APN written agreement where applicable
institutional, agency or provider protocols and policies
observed_facts: Search result text frames nursing authority as dependent on professional scope, applicable rules, a valid order or APN agreement where applicable, and institutional protocols.
Direct page open returned HTTP 403; contents are not independently verified.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Obtain the current Board guidance and applicable current regulations through an authorized public retrieval route; then request the hospital’s nursing policy and order/privilege workflow through authorized institutional access.
limitations: General scope guidance does not identify which RWJUH or Saint Peter’s role can execute a particular ED-to-admission action.
The opened page could not be inspected; access status and exact wording need verification.

sources.title: Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
sources.geography: RWJUH, New Brunswick, Middlesex County, New Jersey
sources.grain: Facility-level public description and service/location information
observed_facts: The page identifies RWJUH at 1 Robert Wood Johnson Place, New Brunswick, NJ 08901.
It describes RWJUH as a Level I trauma center and identifies selected services.
The page is not a medical staff bylaws, credentialing, or clinical authority document.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the public facility page only to anchor facility identity. For the matrix, request current medical staff bylaws, credentialing/privileging rules, ED and admitting service policies, and delegation/supervision policies through authorized institutional channels; record version dates and effective intervals.
limitations: No public role-by-action authority or credential-expiry data found on the inspected page.
Public service descriptions do not establish any individual’s privileges.
Saint Peter’s equivalent facility documents were not located within the search/open limit.

missing_inputs: Current medical staff bylaws and privilege delineation for RWJUH and Saint Peter’s, including emergency department, consultation and admission authority by role and service.
Current facility policies for APP supervision/delegation, nursing orders, escalation and handoff, including setting-specific rules and any required supervisor coverage or ratios.
Authorized, minimum-necessary credential records for simulation roles: license/certification status, facility appointment, granted privileges, effective dates, restrictions, and expiry/renewal dates.
Faculty-approved workflow definition: ED evaluation, order entry, disposition decision, admission acceptance, and inpatient handoff, specifying which actions are in scope.
Current, directly retrievable versions of state statutes and regulations relevant to physician, PA, APN, RN and other included roles; search-result snippets alone are insufficient evidence.
simulation_use: Create a provisional evidence-linked matrix for one RWJUH ED-to-admission workflow with columns role, action, setting, eligibility, supervisor requirement/count, source, effective dates, and status. Mark New Jersey role-scope constraints as public rules pending current-source verification; mark facility privileges, admission acceptance authority, and credential expiry as unresolved institutional inputs. Leave eligibility unknown where evidence does not establish it; do not infer authority from NPI or public role descriptions.
limitations: Scope limited to two searches and four opened pages, with primary official sources only.
Two state pages could not be directly inspected due to 403 responses; their search-result summaries are leads requiring verification.
No dataset was acquired, downloaded, or queried. A source listing is discovery only.
No quantitative local authority or credential dataset was identified. National/external benchmarks were not substituted because they cannot establish New Jersey or facility authority.
